builds.autopilotDescription: Written into .sitesmith/direction.md as the first field, before anything else: near-white ground, one saturated blue accent, Inter at every size, a centred h1 reading "Industrisymaskiner, gennemgået fra bunden" over a subline and two buttons (Se maskinerne / Ring til os), then a thin strip of three trust items. Then three equal rounded cards in a row, one per machine, each with a small line-drawn icon in a rounded square, a name, three bullets and a price with a filled button. Then a four-step "Sådan gør vi" band with numbered circles 01 to 04, then an FAQ accordion, then a dark footer holding the phone number. The clever move would be a dashed border on the cards standing in for a line of stitching and a needle icon that swings on hover. Type: Inter 700 headings, Inter 400 body, small tracked uppercase mono eyebrows. None of it was built.
builds.chosen: Thesis 2 of 4, "a telephone call written down: what the workshop would tell you on 97 22 08 41, in the order it comes out, with the numbers left in". Axis: who the page is spoken from. Thesis 1, the rebuild log, was ranked first and is the one argued in the runner-up block; it was not built because it speaks from the bench outward and treats the buyer as an audience for the workshop's care, while the call speaks from the buyer inward and treats the machine as something handed over to his floor. The eight hours under load, the warranty boundary, the van and the part exchange all survive inside a call; the buyer's own room, his old machine and the 900 kr to move a machine to him do not survive inside a log, and the brief says he does not want to be educated.
builds.paletteReasoning: The count was not fixed in advance and no value was given a role name. The question asked was what a machine-reconditioning workshop is physically coloured, and the answer is: a laminate bench top the machines stand on, tailor's chalk, cast iron under the paint, bare steel of needle bar and throat plate, the scribe line on the bench, the enamel the frames are resprayed in, and oil in the sight glass. That is seven, all low chroma. The only object in that room with a colour of its own is the thread rack, so three thread colours were taken from it, one per machine, because there are three machines. Ten values, three of them saturated, which is deliberately not the one-saturated-accent default the skill names. Named --laminatbord, --kridt, --stobejern, --staal, --rids, --maskinlak, --olie, --traad-karmoisin, --traad-marine, --traad-mos. Contrast was measured before use, not after: ink on ground 14.1:1, staal 5.27:1, olie 4.68:1, kridt on maskinlak 8.19:1, and the three thread colours 5.27, 7.03 and 5.16 on the ground. The thread colours are never set on the enamel, where crimson falls to 1.4:1, which is why the drawings sit on a chalk field and not on the plate. builds.signatureKind: Kind named before building: a machine part drawn head on. Rejected first, explicitly, as the kind this medium reaches for on anything to do with sewing: a dashed border standing in for a line of stitching. Also rejected: a needle-and-thread icon, and a horizontal bar encoding a quantity as width. What was built is nålefeltet (.naalefelt): a wide chalk field under each machine's enamel name plate holding a head-on drawing of the needle bar, presser foot, throat plate and two layers of material, all three drawn to one construction and one set of stroke weights so they can be held against each other, with the only difference being the thing the brief states (one needle bar and a whole foot, a foot in two parts at different heights, or two needle bars with a split between them). The machine's thread colour runs from the guide, through the eye of the needle, into the material and out of the right edge of the field, where it continues at full page width as the 3px rule that closes that machine's entry. The divider is the thread that is in the needle. The Brother, being twin needle, closes on a double rule. Swapped for the category default, a photo card with an icon, the page would lose the only thing that tells the three machines apart at a glance and the three thread colours would become decoration.
builds.secondSwapChanged: The second swap handed the plan to a three-person payroll bureau in Aarhus with three service tiers. The drawings and the thread colours died at once, correctly, but two things survived that should not have: the conversational section order, and the bracket with an exclusion outside it, which any business with a scope could use. Both were changed. The section order stopped being a conversation template and became the machine's direction of travel, out from the Herning floor to the buyer's floor, so the closing move is reversed rather than repeated: the part exchange is the only right-aligned, mirrored block on the page, because it is the only thing moving back towards the workshop. The bracket now labels four named operations that only exist because a machine was taken apart, so it cannot be lifted off this page. (The first swap, to a neighbouring workshop in the same trade with five machines, had already forced a change: almost everything survived, so the plan was bound to the stock. There are three thread colours because there are three machines, the opening line is the count, and the page ends when the machines end.)

builds.autopilotDescription: Nær-sort skærm cirka #0d1117, Inter til alt, mono-versaler med brede sperringer til etiketter. Topbjælke med logo, klokkeslæt og fire KPI-fliser (61 stationer, 4 afvigelser, 3 montører, næste vagtskifte). Under den en todeling: venstre en sorterbar stationstabel med farvet prik yderst til venstre og grønne, gule og røde statuspiller; højre en sidebjælke med tre montørkort med initial-avatarer og en Send montør-knap der åbner en modal. 8px afrundede kort, hårfine #1f2937-streger, tabulartal, og som det kloge greb en sparkline med de seneste aflæsninger i hver række. Skrevet ned som første felt i direction.md og ikke bygget.
builds.chosen: Tese 3, mosaiktavlen: 61 felter der aldrig flytter sig, hvor afvigelse er mærker stemplet på feltet og ikke en farve. Aksen er hvor afvigelsen bor, altså på pladen frem for i rækkefølgen. Tese 2 (tværsnit af nettet, 61 spænd mellem fremløb og retur på én fælles temperaturakse) var højest rangeret og er argumenteret ordentligt i Case for the runner-up; den tabte fordi et vandret spænd på en akse er en måler, og fordi et sorteret akse-felt flytter stationerne rundt hver gang tallene ankommer, mens brieffen siger at skærmen bruges af folk der kender nettet.
builds.paletteReasoning: Spørgsmålet var hvad faget faktisk er farvet af, ikke hvor mange værdier en side skal bruge. Fjernvarme er farvet af rør: et præisoleret fjernvarmerør er sort PE-kappe udenpå, gult PUR-skum indeni og et stålmedierør i midten, og på ethvert rørskema i faget tegnes fremløb rødt og retur blåt. Det giver --skum (bund), --kappe (blæk og mærker), --stål (streger, skravering, mindste etiketter), --fremløb og --retur. Tallet fem faldt ud af rørets tværsnit plus skemaets to farver, ikke af en rolleliste. To af de fem er mættede, ikke én, hvilket er den default SKILL.md navngiver. Ingen af dem betyder status: rødt betyder fremløb og blåt betyder retur på alle 61 plader, også de rolige, så en farve der bærer betydning bruges ikke til andet. Alarm bæres i stedet af mærker. Målt mod --skum: --kappe 14,0:1, --stål 4,8:1, --fremløb 5,2:1, --retur 6,4:1. Rørfarverne bruges bevidst ikke inde i det sorte bånd, fordi de ikke holder 4,5:1 på sort.
builds.signatureKind: Tegnemærker stemplet på et felt, altså en påtegning på en tegning, ikke en graf. Arten blev navngivet før den blev bygget og valgt ved at forkaste den art mediet rækker ud efter først: et dashboard griber først måleren, søjlen, sparklinen og prikken, og det højest rangerede forslag (61 spænd på én fælles temperaturakse) er en måler i forklædning, så det blev kasseret alene af den grund. Mærkesættet er tre mærker der kan optræde samtidig: kasse om returrækken når retur er over 45, kile i hjørnet der peger opad når trykket er over 0,9 og nedad når det er under 0,3, og skravering hen over hele pladen når aflæsningen er ældre end 20 minutter. Byttet ud med kategoriens ene farvede prik ville siden miste hvilken af tre fejl, hvor mange samtidig, og hvilken vej trykket brød.
builds.secondSwapChanged: Swap 2 gav planen til en fragtterminal med 61 porte og tre trucks, altså andet fag, samme gulv. Formen overlevede uændret (fast rutenet af enheder, tre mærker for tre fejlregler, udkald inde i enheden), hvilket betyder at planen var en proces og ikke et design. Derfor blev pladen lavet om: den er nu bygget om rørparret, med Frem i rødt sat direkte over Retur i blåt i samme kolonne og med samme venstrekant og samme højrestillede tal, så hver plade læses som de to rør oven på hinanden, og med differenstryk og alder skubbet ned under en streg som en fodlinje. En terminalport har ikke et par, så terminalen ville skulle tegne pladen forfra. Swap 1 (naboselskab med 210 stationer og seks montører) fjernede den planlagte sortering efter alvorlighed og bandt tavlen til præcis 61 faste pladser uden paginering.

builds.autopilotDescription: Written first, before anything else, as the first field of the direction record. Honest version: a pale parchment ground around #FAF7F2, near-black ink, one muted brass or oxblood accent; a large high-contrast serif (Playfair or Fraunces) in the hero carrying "Håndværk siden 1998" centred in a lot of air, above it a wide-tracked uppercase mono eyebrow "ORGELVÆRKSTED / THY" separated by a hairline rule; below that three equal rounded cards headed "Det laver vi", each with a heading and two lines; under those a figure strip set in tabular numerals: 1998, 4 til 5, 8 til 18 måneder; the clever move a stroke-only SVG organ facade at 8% opacity top right, plus one scroll fade-in; closing with a centred contact block and the phone number set large, foot in the same parchment as the top. None of it was built: no mono, no uppercase eyebrows, no hairlines, no figure strip, no three-card grid, no line drawing, no parchment ground, no scroll fade.
builds.chosen: Thesis 2, "Vindvejen": the page is read in the order the air travels through the instrument, from the bellows to the mouth of the pipe, with the tracker action running the other way. Axis: where the page's order comes from. The wind path is something the parish council can walk up to its own gallery and check; the workshop daybook (thesis 1) and the letter (thesis 3) are ordered only by the sender's paperwork and politeness. The runner-up argued in the record is thesis 1, the daybook: it makes duration visible, which is the council's real worry over an eight to eighteen month job, and a journal notes rather than sells. It loses because the brief forbids parish names and instrument names, so a daybook has empty pages, and because it drags the page towards mono labels, hairlines and tabular figures.
builds.paletteReasoning: The count was never fixed in advance and no colour was given a role. The question asked was what this trade is actually coloured, and an organ workshop turns out to be polychrome and to work in two temperature families at once: warm alum leather, hot hide glue and oak against cold spotted tin and lead, plus exactly one small strong colour, the red felt in the tracker action. Seven fell out of that list: --bælgskind #B9AB93 (old bellows leather, the page ground), --nyt-alunlæder #E3D9C4 (the new white leather going on), --sod-og-jern #191512 (soot and iron fittings, the ink), --orgelmetal #45484E (spotted pipe metal), --hudlim #6E3D0E (hot hide glue), --rødt-filt #7E1A1A (felt punchings), --vindladens-eg #3A2717 (wind chest oak). Two are saturated (hide glue s=0.77, red felt s=0.66), deliberately not the one-saturated-accent default the file calls out. Contrast was measured before any paragraph was set: hide glue reaches only 3.98 on the ground, so it is a surface and never a text colour, with light text on it at 6.41; pipe metal is 4.07 on the ground, under 4.5, so it carries no body text at all, only material. Ground is mid-dark, relative luminance 0.415, not the near-white the category reaches for.
builds.signatureKind: Kind named before it was built: a worn surface. Specifically the fold of a bellows rib, `.bælgfold`, four full-width bands built from a vertical gradient (oak through pipe metal to alum leather at the crest and back) plus a 3px dashed stitch line at the crest, with the inward fold the same surface reversed. Three kinds the medium reaches for first were named and rejected: a stroke-only SVG line drawing, a large sentence set free in air, and a horizontal CSS gauge encoding a quantity as width, the last because SKILL.md names it as the one three builds landed on in three costumes. The page contains zero img and zero svg elements.
builds.secondSwapChanged: Swap 1 (neighbouring organ workshop) left the wind path, the part names and the fold intact, which proved they belong to the trade and not to this client, so the page was bound to the facts only these two have and the condition report was moved from a subordinate clause to the final surface. Swap 2 (same plan, a two-person bookkeeping firm on another floor) held, and that was the failure: ground in the material's colour, repeated bands as separators, sections named after the object's parts, free first meeting at the end is a process, not a drawing, and it could be run on anything. So the plan was changed: the fold stopped being a separator and became the rhythm of the argument. An outward fold precedes what the workshop gives; an inward fold precedes what it costs the council in time or what the workshop refuses to do; the page ends on an outward fold. That alternation only means anything when the limits are themselves the sales argument, which is true here because two people, four or five instruments a year and a flat no to electronic organs are what make eight to eighteen months credible. A bookkeeping firm cannot use it, so the plan can no longer be carried forward to the next job.
